recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It is a narrow active-source correction that aligns the current messaging narrative with the published Jira disposition without changing the later zero-or-more response-message model.
issue_request: FHIR-25465 was Published as Persuasive with Modification for FHIR-core messaging. It requested changing the Message Exchange Patterns text from an absolute one-or-more response-message expectation to typical response messages and clarifying that some notification scenarios may rely on an HTTP response, with the accepted modification naming a response such as 200 possibly accompanied by OperationOutcome.
initial_application: Historical commit 6fc70e07455baeec9c2f599e9d1d1dc03edd308c applied the main source change in source/messaging.html, but the notification sentence omitted the accepted 200 example and remained unclear as 'it reasonable to only expect either only an http response'.
additional_context: source/messaging.html is active current-build narrative via source/hierarchy.xml. Later related decisions FHIR-25252, FHIR-40518, and FHIR-27544 support the same model that a bare HTTP acknowledgement can be enough when no message Bundle payload is needed, and the later zero-or-more response-message changes do not conflict with this narrow clarification. Confluence minutes confirmed the FHIR-I vote and rationale; no direct Zulip hit for FHIR-25465 was found, but a later related Zulip thread supports the same interpretation.
reconciliation: Updated source/messaging.html to say: 'For some notification scenarios it is reasonable to expect only an HTTP response (e.g. 200), possibly accompanied by an OperationOutcome.'
source_changes: source/messaging.html: clarified the notification scenario sentence to use HTTP response wording, include the 200 example, and remove the stale ambiguous 'either only an http response' phrasing.
